findings.text: the fragment says the unreadable-ledger case fails at c34d88cc "because the read failure was reduced to an absent ledger and the target was refused as an unknown run", but the log it names shows `reckon._store.CorruptEnvelopeError` escaping uncaught from `_require_repairs_target`; that is the other damage shape, since a `LedgerError` is what the old handler reduced to an absent ledger, so the record states a cause its own receipt refutes, which is the misattribution this section exists to remove.

the base-arm row and the paragraph at :141 present "4 failed, 30 passed" as the same cases measured on both arms, but that log collects 34 tests against the head arm's 35 because it predates the unreadable-ledger case, so the delivered file's fifth `--repairs` case is measured only in the c34d88cc arm and the two arms differ by the test file as well as by the change under test.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 9e727bd0 — c710b880 carries the option, the admission check, the pointer field and the promotion branch; c34d88cc adds the fragment and figure; abfef36e closes the unreadable-ledger path; 707e852b records that repair in the fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks that a dispatch naming a promoted run promote with the impl move exempt; tests/test_dispatch_declares_the_run_it_repairs.py:193 drives that through `crew.complete` and asserts the reason `corrective-run:repairs:<id>`, and the manifest records the head arm at logs/head-arm.txt (35 passed, EXIT=0) over the base arm at logs/base-arm.txt (4 failed, EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is the §4 `--repairs RUN_ID` declaration; reckon/cli.py:1309 adds the option, reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3290 admits the target before launch, reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4827 records it on the pointer, and reckon/crew/promotion.py:4221 exempts the impl move, which is what the goal states.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names four arms, each with a revision header, an exit status and a log path, and its claimed head 707e852b was the worktree's HEAD with a clean status; the worktree has since been reclaimed on promotion, and the four commits stay reachable from the main checkout's HEAD.
item_verdicts.write_paths: `git diff --numstat 9e727bd0 707e852b` lists exactly the six paths the manifest declares, and every count sits in the added column.

justifications.durability: tests/test_dispatch_declares_the_run_it_repairs.py:262 reddens on the pre-fix head and on a swallow regression, but no committed test drives the CLI forwardings at reckon/cli.py:1454 and :1542, so dropping either leaves the suite green.
justifications.evidence: the head arm measures the done_when and is recorded (logs/head-arm.txt 35 passed at 707e852b, logs/new-case-at-delivered-head.txt red at c34d88cc), but the fragment's prose at :114 states a failure mechanism its own named log contradicts and its base-arm row at :133 offers a 34-test arm as the delivered file.
justifications.fit: the branch at reckon/crew/promotion.py:4217 sits beside the attempt-kind branch it mirrors, reuses the corrective-run reason prefix, and reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4132 catches the store error beside the ledger error instead of adding a refusal shape.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/promotion.py:4221 reads the recorded `repairs` and returns the exemption with reason `corrective-run:repairs:<run_id>`, so the declared repair promotes through `crew.complete` with no `--no-impl-change`.
justifications.scope_discipline: `git diff --numstat 9e727bd0 707e852b` lists exactly the six paths the manifest declares, with no deleted line on any of them.
